@@ -0,0 +1,17 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8880'
+title: 'Qwen3.8 MTP verify attention: size blocks for long context like decode attention'
+---
+## Why
+From 2k to 64k, a 4-token verify grows by 6.2 ms, about twice the KV-read floor. Plain decode grows by 3.2 ms, which is at the floor. Verify attention uses at most 16 blocks × 4 KV heads, which is 64 threadgroups. Decode attention uses 32–128 blocks of 128 keys.
+
+## What
+In `VerifyAttentionKernel.swift`, choose the split-K block count from the context length in the same way as the decode attention kernel. That gives more threadgroups at long context and a cheaper reduce.
+
+## Acceptance
+- [ ] Microbench: 4-token verify attention at 2k, 32k and 64k, before and after.
+- [ ] `qwencheck.sh`: MTP greedy ids identical to the golden file, including the 32k prompt, and cache reuse passes. Any id change must be justified as a bf16 near-tie under 0.5 logit gap and recorded on this card.
+- [ ] All five bundles are green. `qwenbench.sh` delta on this card. #qwen-perf
\ No newline at end of file

@@ -1,6 +1,33 @@
 ---
 assignees:
 - claude-code
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m7jv9cxafpk71bzax9ntgz1s
+  text: |-
+    Research + microbench (blocker). Picked up at HEAD 46a43005.
+
+    Microbench = existing opt-in suite VerifyAttentionBlockPassProfileTests (16 layers, own caches, bf16, median of 9), MLX_VERIFY_ATTENTION_PROFILE_KEYS=2048,32768,65536, sweep b4..b128. Script: scratchpad/vaprofile.sh, output scratchpad/vaprofile_before_117ymn8.txt. Whole verify attention (block + combine), ms over 16 layers:
+
+    | keys | rows | b4 | b8 | **b16 (current)** | b32 | b64 | b128 (decode rule) | decode floor |
+    |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+    | 2k | 4 | 1.62 | 1.52 | 1.51 | 1.65 | 1.64 | 1.61 | 1.27 |
+    | 2k | 5 | 1.47 | 1.45 | 1.48 | 1.69 | 1.56 | 1.79 | |
+    | 32k | 4 | 6.59 | 4.36 | **3.93** | 4.20 | 4.39 | 4.70 | 2.86 |
+    | 32k | 5 | 6.84 | 4.77 | **4.42** | 4.61 | 4.80 | 5.39 | |
+    | 64k | 4 | 12.09 | 7.82 | **6.93** | 7.60 | 7.57 | 7.92 | 5.14 |
+    | 64k | 5 | 12.88 | 8.50 | **7.88** | 8.06 | 8.27 | 9.08 | |
+
+    Current rule picks 4 blocks at 2k, 16 at 32k and 64k. The combine pass (the "reduce") costs 0.10-0.17 ms over 16 layers at b16: it is not where the excess is.
+
+    Finding: the premise of the card does not hold on this M5 Ultra (64 GPU cores). 16 blocks x 4 KV heads = 64 threadgroups = exactly one per core, and each threadgroup holds ~28 KB of threadgroup memory (3 tiles of 16 keys x 264 bf16 + score exchange), so only one is resident per core. More blocks only add a second wave plus more block results. The decode-like rule (128 blocks at 32k/64k) is 14-22% SLOWER for rows 4 and 5; b32 is 4-10% slower. At 2k all counts are within noise (~0.1 ms over 16 layers).
+
+    What did not work (reverted): 8-key bf16 tiles (halfTileKeys 16 -> 8, half the threadgroup memory, so two threadgroups can share a core) with the same sweep (scratchpad/vaprofile_bk8_117ymn8.txt): b16 rows 4 at 64k is 6.93 again, rows 5 is 8.26, and b32 does not beat 16-key tiles at b16 for any row count. So more resident threadgroups do not help either.
+
+    Where the excess is: cost goes with the SIMD-group matrices per threadgroup, not the key count per block. At 64k b16: rows 2 (2 matrices) 5.15 ms = decode floor; rows 3 and 4 (3 matrices) 6.93 ms both; rows 5 (4 matrices) 7.88 ms. The excess over the floor is the per-matrix work (score + value matmuls, online softmax) inside each threadgroup, which no block count changes.
+
+    No code changed. Implementing the card as written would regress MTP decode at 32k/64k. Need a decision: (a) drop/close the card, (b) re-scope to the per-matrix cost (e.g. fewer matrices per key tile for rows 3-5, a cheaper softmax/exchange step), or (c) make the block count follow the GPU core count (blocks = cores / kvHeads), which keeps b16 here but avoids 1.6 waves on a 40-core M5 Max. qwencheck/qwenbench/test suites were not run, because nothing changed.
+  timestamp: 2026-11-16T18:53:07.370796+00:00
